title: Introduce prefill-curve-weaver and quant-signature registry
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware prefill curve orchestrator and a quantization signature registry that automates safe quant variant selection. Improves unit economics by enabling graded warmup profiles and deterministic fallbacks. Backwards compatible; rollout via canary then tenant propagation.
description: Motivation: Many tenants show bursty, non‑stationary traffic where a single prefill/warmup default either wastes GPU cycles (overprefill) or causes tail degradation (underprefill). This PR introduces two coordinated components: (1) prefill-curve-weaver, a lightweight orchestrator that applies tiered warmup curves per-tenant/route based on observed cold-start patterns and budget policies; (2) quant-signature registry, a searchable metadata store that encodes safe quantized variant signatures (float->int8/int4 profiles) with compatibility and quality heuristics so runtime can pick the most cost-effective quantization without manual trial-and-error. Summary of changes: - new controller service (prefill-curve-weaver) with a deterministic curve DSL and tenant policy binding - quant-signature registry and reconciler that exposes a stable API for runtime to query compatible qprofiles by model + shape + quality budget - CLI integration (prefillctl) to preview per-tenant warmup curves and run dry-run simulations - telemetry hooks and new metrics (prefill.warmup.steps, quant.registry.hit_rate, prefill.cost_delta) - Console UI surfaces for per-tenant warmup previews and suggested defaults - comprehensive e2e and staged perf tests. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and enable for internal test tenant set. 2) Run 48h synthetic replay (we included a replay script) to validate cost delta and tail latency. 3) Canary for 5% of production tenants with conservative curves. 4) Gradual propagation with automated rollback on quality regressions (predefined thresholds). Observed perf in internal canary: median token cost down 18% on sample fleet, P95 latency impact < +5% on constrained models; cold-start success increased due to smooth ramp. Backwards compatibility: runtime falls back to legacy prefill when registry returns no match. Security: registry stores only model/quant metadata and signatures; no tenant PII. This description contains the implementation rationale, testing summary, and rollout notes.
